summary: Intermittent OCSP stapling validation failures when egress routed through AZ-local HTTP CONNECT proxy causing artifact 502s and model pull integrity errors
description: Issue summary: Customer (Aurelia Healthtech, private deployment) reports intermittent 502 errors and occasional integrity failures on large model shard downloads. Failures correlate with requests egressing from specific AZs that route traffic through the corporate HTTP CONNECT appliance. Impact: model pulls fail ~5-15% of attempts in affected AZs, causing serving node fallback to smaller model variants and increased latencies for production traffic. Observed when pulling >50MB ranged shard streams or long-lived gRPC/tls connections used for serving runtime model startup.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy private agent in Aurelia VPC in us-east-1a with default egress routing through corporate edge appliance
Trigger model rollout requiring new shard download (e.g., scale-up job or cold start of redwood-open-gpt-3b)
Observe repeated ranged GETs over HTTP/2 for large shard files; intermittent 502s and TLS verification errors in serving logs
Move egress to allowed direct internet path or VPCE for same agent — issue does not reproduce
logs: 2026-03-09T14:23:11Z serving-node-7f: GET /shards/redwood-open-gpt-3b/part-12 range:bytes=0-52428800 -> 502 from origin-cdn (upstream-alpn: h2 -> negotiated by proxy: http/1.1)
2026-03-09T14:23:11Z control-plane: artifact-fetch error: tls: certificate validation failed: no OCSP staple (responder timeout)
2026-03-09T14:23:12Z agent: retrying shard download (attempt 2) via same egress -> succeeded after switching to different AZ egress path
pcap-snippet: PROXY injected 'Proxy-Authorization' and converted ALPN h2 to http/1.1 during CONNECT; OCSP stapling TLS extension status_request absent on server handshake when proxied
comments: Aisha Khan (Support): Customer reported spikes in 502s when they rotated model versions yesterday evening. They see ~10% failure rate for artifactory range requests from us-east-1a. Logged with support at 2026-03-09 14:30 UTC.

Liam Torres (SRE): Started packet captures from an affected agent. Early signal: proxy rewrites ALPN and appears to terminate TLS for connection reuse; OCSP stapling not presented to the client in proxied flows.

Customer (Aurelia): Confirmed that when we route through our corporate egress appliance the downloads fail; if we route via a temporary NAT gateway that bypasses the appliance downloads succeed consistently.
Liam Torres (SRE): Adding control-plane tolerant retry for artifact fetches in PR #7891 while we validate network-side fixes. Will monitor for reduced surface area. (see related_github_prs entry)
Support Engineering: Suggested workaround published to customer: add our artifact CDN IP ranges to allowlist or configure egress to use VPCE for artifact fetches.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: Corporate HTTP CONNECT/transparent proxy is performing TLS termination or ALPN rewrite which interferes with OCSP stapling and HTTP/2 range semantics required by our CDN for resumable shard downloads.

Evidence: pcaps show upstream Server Hello missing status_request extension when proxied; OCSP responder timeouts correlate with proxied flows only. ALPN downgraded from h2 to http/1.1 in proxied connections, and origin chose chunked/connection-close response leading to range merge issues.
Reproducibility: Deterministic when egress flows through the appliance in affected AZs. Bypassing the proxy or switching egress removes the failure.
Temporary mitigation tested: control-plane retry logic with exponential backoff + reattempt on alternate egress path reduced immediate customer impact while network team applies fix.
resolution_notes: Workaround & next steps: (1) Customer applied allowlist of artifact CDN ASN/IP ranges and routed artifact fetches via VPCE—this eliminated errors. (2) SRE published PR #7891 to add additional artifact-fetch retry with ALPN-tolerant fallback and a short backoff window; deployed to prod agents as canary on 2026-03-12. (3) Network team agreed to change appliance config to enable TLS passthrough for bucket/cdn hostnames and preserve ALPN and status_request extension. Follow-up: validate week-long telemetry for error rate in affected AZs and close ticket after 72h of stability. Postmortem required if errors reoccur after network change.
next_steps: Network: confirm TLS passthrough rollout schedule with Aurelia network ops (ETA 2026-03-14)
SRE: observe artifact fetch success rate for 72 hours post-fix; if >99.9% close incident
Support: update runbook with explicit guidance for customers using egress appliances (include allowlist CIDR and VPCE recommendation)
